stack_detection.signature: New-Object -ComObject Word.Application -> REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG 0x80040154 (no Office installed; Excel likewise); no LibreOffice present

channel_setup: Attempted to provision LibreOffice for the UNO fallback: (1) winget machine install -> UAC consent dialog on the secure desktop, unreachable by any non-elevated agent BY DESIGN; (2) MSI per-user (MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1) -> exit 0 no-op, package is machine-scope only; (3) msiexec /a administrative extraction -> 1618 ERROR_INSTALL_ALREADY_RUNNING, the Windows Installer service is locked by the original msiexec still parked behind the unanswered UAC prompt.

t1_read_text.detail: Blocked: no office application installed and none installable without a human answering UAC.

measurements.notes: Environmental block, not a channel property — Word-via-COM is proven technology (three decades of automation) and the family result is already established cross-OS (UNO on Linux 21 tok/65x, Pages on macOS 21 tok, Shell.Application on Windows 28 tok in windows-explorer-object-model). The genuine routing datum here: an AUTONOMOUS agent on Windows cannot cross a UAC consent dialog (secure desktop, unreachable by SendInput/UIA at any integrity level below the prompt's) — and a UAC prompt left unanswered locks the whole Windows Installer service (1618) for every subsequent MSI operation. Provisioning software is a human-in-the-loop step; agents must detect the pending-consent state (consent.exe process present) and queue, not retry. RESOLVED SAME DAY, with one last routing datum: the user clicked the UAC dialog and installed Office — the completed star cell is windows-word-object-model.json (18 tok vs 1446, 80x). The LibreOffice MSI itself never landed: the consent the user granted belonged to an msiexec whose parent (winget) we had already killed — an elevation granted to an ORPHANED request installs nothing, silently. Lesson: after any elevated step, verify the artifact (files/registry), never the click. UNO on Windows left unrun rather than re-raising a UAC prompt; the UNO family is already measured twice on Linux and Word covers Tier C here.

permissions_required: one human click on the UAC consent dialog (secure desktop)
